newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Loss of Asian farmland will not raise prices-study.
newsitem.headline: Loss of Asian farmland will not raise prices-study.

text.p: The rapid conversion of agricultural land in the Asia-Pacific region will have a negligible impact on world food prices, experts from the region said on Tuesday.
"Concerns over loss of land due to urbanisation are unwarranted," a study presented to the Pacific Basin Economic Council (PBEC) in Manila said.
"Estimates of these losses based on current urban densities are quite small and have a negligible impact on world prices over the 1992-2005 projection."
Restrictions on textiles and clothing in North America had forced some Asian economies to pour more labour and capital into the food and agriculture sectors.

"Failure to fully reform (North America's) Multifibre Agreement will force more labour and capital into the food and agriculture sectors in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines, resulting in a $4.5 billion increase in net exports of foods products from that region by the year 2005," the study said.
"Trade is a two-way street, and obstacles to exports from Asia will come back to haunt those sectors seeking to export to this region," it added.
